input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results and a read of the entire Agreement (including the General Provisions in Section 14) confirms there is no insurance obligation anywhere. Kubient is a hosting/ad-tech services vendor that collects, maintains and stores visitor information (Section 9(b)(iii)) and indemnifies Customer broadly (Section 10(a)), so the absence of any coverage falls into the rule's walk-away territory (no insurance for a vendor processing personal data). We therefore inserted the preferred coverage package as a new Section 14(j): CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Customer data is processed, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request, and flagged the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) in the comment as a landing zone.

ops.text: (j) Kubient shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the Term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Kubient collects, processes or stores Customer data (including visitor information), cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; together with workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law. Kubient shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer on request.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance provision, so we added standard coverage (CGL, E&O and cyber, plus statutory workers' compensation) with certificates on request, consistent with Kubient's collection and storage of visitor data under Section 9(b)(iii). If helpful, we can accept reduced limits of USD 1,000,000 E&O and USD 2,000,000 cyber.
proposal.summary: Insert vendor insurance provision in General Provisions
